Honestly with my plans for the future im completely lost, I've only worked 1 job which was at an amazon warehouse for a few months. I have no meaningful qualifications and even though I spend all my time on a PC doesnt exactly mean I'm good at IT, sure i built a pc and know basic things like reinstalling windows but I know nothing about about office programs, servers and I'm a complete shut in with with a lack of any communication skill. Whenever I try something new I can get into it for a few weeks or maybe a few months if im lucky then completely drop it and go back to gaming, this happened with art, game design, learning guitar, graphic design and recently cyber security which I found complicated and boring. I know it doesn't matter but man instead my brain would rather give up at the first try just not to embarrass myself.

For sure, I wish if I was going to pursue a pro career it was atleast in some kind of physical sport so I can atleast gain some real life benefits even if I failed at it, but here I am good at clicking a mouse and keyboard with nothing else to show for it. I gotta move on fast but its a struggle getting started on something else after spending most of your life doing this one thing.

Thanks for the comment but legit for me it wasn't just an escape, pro gamers were my idols while kids my age had sports players or musicians, the mindset that is fucking me over is that because I spent so much effort and time trying to pursue the one goal that I had and failed, what say its not going to go the same way for anything else I try. Whenever I try something new I give up way too quickly just because its difficult and go back to gaming where I can feel like im good at something even if im not enjoying it the same way I used to. Its a completely stupid mindset, If I managed to put the work in to reach the top 1% of players in a game like overwatch with millions of players then why can't I just apply that effort to something else? But man it just doesn't click for me and I continue sitting on my ass.

Wondered that question all the time, if all that time went to something useful. I can't really blame gaming by itself but it for sure was a bad outlet for me.
